title: C# Question & Answers - Iterators
description: This section of our 1000+ C# MCQs focuses on iterators in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: What is an iterator?
questions.explanation: In C#, an iterator is a method, get accessor, or operator that uses yield return (or yield break) to produce a sequence. The compiler builds a state machine that implements IEnumerator / IEnumerable.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code snippet?
questions.explanation:
GetEnumerator plus yield return makes MyClass usable in foreach. Console.Write prints each character followed by a space.

Output:

A B C D

questions.question: Choose the correct statements for the following C# code?

options.text: Implements the GetEnumerator() method defined by IEnumerable
The yield return statement returns the next object in the collection, which in this case is the next character in chrs

questions.explanation: This iterator method is named GetEnumerator, which is what foreach looks for (the pattern-based equivalent of IEnumerable.GetEnumerator). Each yield return produces the next char from chrs. The class does not have to list : IEnumerable explicitly for foreach to work if GetEnumerator is public.

questions.question: What does the yield return statement specify in the following C# code snippet?

options.text: returns the next object in the collection
Both returns the output & returns the next object in the collection

questions.explanation: yield return pauses the iterator and hands the current value to the consumer. The next MoveNext() resumes after that yield.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code snippet?

options.text:
Iterate the first 7 letters:
   A B C D E F G

   G H I J K L

Iterate the first 7 letters:
   A B C D E F G n
   Iterate letters from F to L:
   H I J K L

questions.explanation:
MyItr(7) yields 'A'+0 through 'A'+6, i.e. A–G. Console.WriteLine("n") prints a literal n (not a newline escape). MyItr(7, 12) yields i = 7..11, i.e. H–L (the prompt text "F to L" does not match those bounds).

Output:

Iterate the first 7 letters:
A B C D E F G n
Iterate letters from F to L:
H I J K L

questions.question: What are the advantages of the named iterator?

options.text: They allow to pass arguments to the iterator that control what elements are obtained
This form of iterators can be overloaded
Both They allow to pass arguments to the iterator that control what elements are obtained & This form of iterators can be overloaded

questions.explanation: A named iterator is a method that returns IEnumerable (not GetEnumerator). You can pass parameters and overload it, as MyItr(int) and MyItr(int, int) do in question 7.
